text: Run any tool at a specific version ad hoc with mise exec, downloading it if needed, without changing config or the current shell
quote: mise downloads Node.js 24 if it is not installed, then runs the command after `--`. This does not change any config file or your current shell's environment.

text: Set a personal global default version for a tool with mise use --global
quote: Set a personal default `mise use --global node@24`

text: Keep multiple versions of runtimes like Node, Python, Ruby and Go on one machine and declare per project which ones to use in mise.toml
quote: Keep multiple versions of Node.js, Python, Ruby, Go, and other tools on the same machine, then declare which ones a project uses in `mise.toml`.

text: mise use installs tools and records the version requests in the project's config file
quote: mise use node@24 python@3.14 ... This installs both tools and records the version requests in the project's config

text: Pin the exact resolved version in config with --pin instead of a fuzzy request
quote: Add `--pin` to write the resolved version instead

text: Reads existing asdf .tool-versions files as-is, so asdf projects work without conversion
quote: Coming from asdf? mise reads `.tool-versions` as-is.

text: Supports idiomatic version files such as .node-version and .ruby-version
quote: mise is also compatible with asdf `.tool-versions` files and with idiomatic version files like `.node-version` and `.ruby-version`.

text: Can still use asdf plugins when needed
quote: mise is compatible with asdf `.tool-versions` files and can still use asdf plugins when needed.

text: Once activated, automatically switches tool versions based on the current directory
quote: Once activated, mise can automatically switch between different versions of tools based on the directory you're in.

text: Per-project environment variables from mise.toml, .env files, secrets and shell commands, set on entering a directory and removed on leaving
quote: Per-project env vars from `mise.toml`, .env files, secrets, and shell commands. Set when you enter, gone when you leave.

text: Add environment variables to the project config from the CLI with mise set
quote: Run `mise set` to add an `[env]` section

text: Shims mode puts tools on PATH for editors and scripts that don't read shell startup files
quote: Shims for editors and scripts that never read your shell startup file

text: Install over 1,000 tools and choose a version per project
quote: Install any of 1,000+ tools, choose a version for each project, and switch automatically as you move between directories.

text: Install tools from multiple backends: package registries like npm and cargo, release hosts like GitHub, or plugins
quote: A backend is where mise installs a tool from: a package registry such as npm or cargo, a release host such as GitHub, or a plugin.

text: Install binaries directly from GitHub releases using github:owner/repo identifiers
quote: A tool without a shorthand can still be installed by its backend identifier, such as `github:owner/repo`

text: Install Python CLI tools from PyPI via pipx and npm packages as global tools
quote: Install claude-code from npm... Install black from PyPI via pipx... Install ripgrep directly from GitHub releases

text: Built-in Homebrew implementation installs formulae and casks without requiring Homebrew
quote: mise has its own Homebrew implementation, so it installs formulae and casks without requiring Homebrew.

text: Short registry names let you install tools without knowing their full backend identifier
quote:
mise use aws-cli

instead of

mise use aqua:aws/aws-cli

text: Override the backend for any tool using MISE_BACKENDS_<TOOL> environment variables, e.g. to use a vfox plugin
quote: You can override the backend for any tool using environment variables with the pattern `MISE_BACKENDS_<TOOL>`.

text: Disable specific backends through a setting
quote: mise settings disable_backends=asdf

text: Install tools from arbitrary HTTP URLs per platform, with checksums
Opt in to current registry data without upgrading the mise executable
quote: Users whose system package manager ships mise updates slowly can opt in to current registry data without replacing the mise executable

text: Fuzzy-search available tools and show their descriptions
quote: mise search jq          # fuzzy-match names and show descriptions

text: Show tools with newer versions and upgrade within the configured version request
quote: Show tools with newer versions `mise outdated` Upgrade within the configured request `mise upgrade node`

text: Show which executable a command resolves to with mise which
quote: Show which executable a command runs `mise which node`

text: List the executables the active tools provide
quote: List the executables the active tools provide

text: Hierarchical config: mise.toml files in parent directories are merged, and deeper files override shallower ones
quote: what is defined there overrides anything set in `~/src/work/mise.toml` or `~/.config/mise.toml`. The config contents are merged.

text: Inspect the loaded config files and the selected tool versions, along with their source files
quote: Run `mise config` to list the config files mise loaded, and `mise ls --current` to see the selected tool versions.

text: Development, test and production config overlays
quote: Development, test, and production overlays

text: Commit a lockfile and install with mise install --locked so every machine and job gets the same versions
quote: Commit a lockfile and install with `mise install --locked`. Every job then installs the same versions

text: Bump lockfile versions with a dry run and JSON output
quote: MISE_SAFE=1 mise lock --bump --dry-run --json

text: Define project tasks in mise.toml for build, test, lint and deploy, run with the project's tools and env vars
quote: A task is a named command or script that runs with your project's tools and environment variables. Use tasks for builds, tests, linters, development servers, and other commands you want teammates and CI to run consistently.

text: Write tasks as standalone executable script files in a mise-tasks directory, with editor syntax highlighting and linting
quote: You can also define tasks as standalone shell scripts. All you have to do is create an `executable` file in a specific directory like `mise-tasks`.

text: Task dependencies run in parallel by default, and dependency-only tasks can group other tasks
quote: A dependency-only task can group other tasks. Prerequisites may run in parallel; their order in `depends` does not establish a sequence

text: mise watch automatically reruns tasks when files change
quote: [mise watch](./running-tasks.html#watching-files) to automatically rebuild on changes—no configuration required, but it helps

text: mise run installs missing tools before a task starts unless auto-install is turned off
quote: `mise run` loads the project's configuration and, unless `task.run_auto_install` is off, installs missing tools before the task starts.

text: Install all tools a project declares with mise install in the project directory
quote: run `mise install` in the project directory and `mise tasks ls` to list its tasks.

text: mise bootstrap sets up a whole machine from one checked-in file: OS packages, repos, dotfiles, shell activation, macOS defaults, services, then tools
quote: mise bootstrap sets up a new computer from the same file: OS packages, git repos, dotfiles, shell activation, macOS defaults, and services, then your tools.

text: Manage dotfiles as symlinks, copies or templates, plus single-line edits
quote: Dotfiles as symlinks, copies, or templates, plus single-line edits

text: Bootstrap remote hosts over SSH
quote: Remote hosts over SSH with `mise bootstrap remote`

text: Clone a bootstrap project from a Git URL and apply it
quote: `--from <GIT_URL>` — Clone a bootstrap project (a Git repository with a mise.toml) and apply it

text: Preview bootstrap changes with a dry run, or inspect them with bootstrap status and plan
quote: Preview with `--dry-run`. To inspect without applying, use `mise bootstrap status` for current state or `mise bootstrap plan`

text: Create, update or remove local Linux users and groups declared in config
quote: Creates, updates, or removes the local accounts declared in `[bootstrap.users]` and `[bootstrap.groups]` on Linux.

text: Exit non-zero when accounts differ from config, for drift checking
quote: `--missing` — Exit with status 1 if any account differs from the config (all are still listed)

text: Manage Docker Compose projects declared in bootstrap config
quote: Manage Docker Compose projects from `[bootstrap.compose]`

text: Set MISE_SAFE=1 so project configuration cannot execute code
quote: set MISE_SAFE=1 so that project configuration cannot execute code.

text: Asks you to trust a repository's config before letting it run code
quote: mise asks before it lets a repository's config run code.

text: Restrict installs to versions older than a minimum release age, defaulting to 24 hours for every backend
quote: A newly published release is malicious | Minimum release age | 24 hours for every backend

text: Automatically verifies Cosign/Minisign signatures, SLSA provenance and GitHub artifact attestations with a built-in implementation
quote: For aqua tools, Cosign/Minisign signatures, SLSA provenance, and GitHub artifact attestations are verified automatically using mise's built-in implementation.

text: Optional sandboxing limits what tasks and commands can read, write or reach, on Linux and macOS
quote: A task or command reads, writes or reaches more than it needs | Sandboxing | Off; Linux and macOS only

text: mise mcp runs an MCP server that lets AI assistants read project tools, tasks, env vars and config, and run tasks
quote: `mise mcp` runs a Model Context Protocol server that lets an AI assistant read a project's tools, tasks, environment variables and config files, and run its tasks.

text: Official mise-action GitHub Action installs mise and the repo's declared tools, and caches them by default
quote: mise-action installs mise and the tools declared in the checked-out repository. By default it also caches the tools

text: A committed wrapper script installs mise on demand, so CI pipelines need no separate install step
quote: A committed wrapper can install mise on demand, avoiding a separate installation step in each pipeline.

text: One-line install script, with support for pinning a specific mise version
quote:
curl https://mise.run | MISE_VERSION="$MISE_VERSION" sh
mise version | grep -q "^${MISE_VERSION#v} "
mise install

text: Run mise as if it were started in another directory with -C/--cd
quote: `-C --cd <DIR>` — Run as if mise were started in DIR
